topic.subject: science
topic.title: Metals and non-metals
topic.scope: physical properties, reactions with oxygen, water, acids, displacement, reactivity, uses, corrosion

concepts.name: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals

misconceptions.statement: All metals are always solid at room temperature.
misconceptions.why: Students generalize from common metals like iron and copper seen in daily life.
misconceptions.fix: Mercury is a metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature.

probe.question: Is mercury a metal?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it is a liquid.

misconceptions.why: Students often associate non-metals with oxygen or nitrogen in the air.
misconceptions.fix: Non-metals can be solids (like carbon or sulfur) or liquids (like bromine) in addition to gases.

probe.question: Is sulfur a non-metal?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it is a solid.

concepts.name: Chemical Reactions with Oxygen and Water

misconceptions.statement: Metal oxides are always acidic in nature.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse metal oxides with non-metal oxides which form acids in water.
misconceptions.fix: Metal oxides are generally basic, while non-metal oxides are generally acidic.

probe.question: What happens when magnesium oxide is dissolved in water and tested with litmus?
probe.wrong_answer: It turns blue litmus red because it is an oxide.

misconceptions.statement: Any metal can displace another metal from its salt solution.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that if a reaction happens between two metals, it will always happen regardless of which is the salt.
misconceptions.fix: Only a more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution.

probe.question: Will copper displace zinc from zinc sulfate solution?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because both are metals and they react.
